subject: math

objective.text: Make arrays with square tiles. Some tiles may be left over. Describe the array with rows and columns.

explanations.title: Groups and tiles left over
explanations.text: Make equal groups of 5 with 17 tiles. You make 3 groups. 2 tiles are left. That is not enough for another group of 5. Put the extra tiles to the side.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (17 tiles in groups of 5)

explanations.title: Groups become rows
explanations.text: Move the equal groups into rows to make an array. 3 groups of 5 make 3 rows of 5. 5 plus 5 plus 5 equals 15.

explanations.title: The same groups become columns
explanations.text: Use the same groups to make columns. Now you see 3 columns of 5. There are still 3 fives. The total is still 15.

explanations.title: Build one row at a time
explanations.text: Put 3 tiles in one row. Keep adding rows of 3 until you have 12 tiles. You made 4 rows of 3. 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 12.

explanations.title: Push rows together, then split into columns
explanations.text: Push the rows together to make one rectangle. Then split it into columns. 4 rows of 3 become 3 columns of 4. The total does not change.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (use rulers to push and separate)

examples.title: 17 tiles in groups of 5
examples.text: 17 tiles make 3 groups of 5 and 2 tiles are left over. The array uses 15 tiles.

examples.title: 3 rows of 5 and 3 columns of 5
examples.text: 3 rows of 5 is 5 plus 5 plus 5 equals 15. 3 columns of 5 is also 5 plus 5 plus 5 equals 15.

examples.title: 4 rows of 3
examples.text: 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 12. Push the rows together and split into columns. You get 3 columns of 4.

examples.title: 3 columns of 4
examples.text: 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 12. 4 rows of 3 and 3 columns of 4 have the same total.
